title: Climate Adaptation in Action: Case Study Evaluating the Role of the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change in Building Resilient Agriculture in Rajasthan, India
content: India is highly vulnerable to climate change, experiencing frequent droughts, floods, and cyclones due to its geographical location and socioeconomic conditions. Climate change exacerbates these socioeconomic issues, affecting agriculture, water resources, and rural livelihoods, particularly in areas where adaptive capacity is limited. Over 60 percent of India's primarily agricultural economy depends on farming, making it sensitive to climatic shifts. India's National Adaptation Fund on Climate Change (NAFCC) serves as a significant tool for financing adaptation projects, highlighting both its potential and limitations. Although the fund has helped integrate adaptation into development planning, its implementation has encountered governance challenges, including procedural delays, weak institutional capacity, and limited participation of vulnerable communities.1 Rajasthan, in northwest India, is especially vulnerable to these impacts due to its arid-to-semi-arid climate with highly variable rainfall, rising temperatures, and desertification, which pose severe risks to agriculture and livelihoods. The state also faces severe water shortages, soil erosion, and declining agricultural productivity—issues that are projected to worsen with ongoing climate change.2
